title: National Highways: network expansion vs construction

verification_claim.text: MoRTH reported that India's National Highway network increased from 91,287 km in 2014 to 146,195 km in 2024-25, an increase of about 60%.

definitions: National Highway network length is the total network classified/notified as National Highways.
An increase in network length is not automatically identical to kilometres of newly constructed road.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
evidence.title: Annual Report 2024-25
evidence.evidence_summary: MoRTH reports total National Highway length of 146,195 km and states that the NH network increased by 60% from 91,287 km in 2014.

research_summary: The official MoRTH annual report states that the National Highway network increased from 91,287 km in 2014 to 146,195 km in 2024-25, approximately 60%. This is a network-length comparison. It should not be rewritten as a claim that exactly 54,908 km of brand-new road were physically constructed, because network length and construction length are different metrics.

locked_claims.text: National Highway network length in 2014 was 91,287 km.
National Highway network length reported for 2024-25 was 146,195 km.
The reported increase in NH network length was about 60%.

material_caveats: Network expansion is not the same metric as newly constructed road length.
The official figure is 146,195 km; changing it to 146,145 km or another nearby value is a factual error.
prohibited_claims: Exactly 54,908 km of brand-new National Highways were constructed between 2014 and 2024-25.
Every kilometre of network increase represents newly built road.
The 2024-25 NH network figure was 146,145 km.
